title: Stripe QuickBooks Integration: How to Connect and Automate Your Accounting in 2026
summary: Learn QuickBooks Stripe integration in 2026, from setup to reconciliation. See how Synder syncs Stripe payments, fees, refunds, and taxes to QuickBooks.
body_markdown:
Stripe doesn’t connect to QuickBooks Online on its own. Every sale, fee, and payout needs a third-party connector to reach your books. If you’re manually matching Stripe’s lump-sum deposits to individual orders, that reconciliation work compounds with every new transaction. This guide walks through connecting the two platforms step by step – with a clearing account setup that keeps revenue, fees, and payouts aligned.


Both per-transaction and daily summary sync modes are covered, along with the most common setup mistakes and how to fix them.


---


## **TL;DR**


- Stripe data reaches QuickBooks Online only through a connector app, such as Intuit’s Stripe Connector by QuickBooks, middleware, or a dedicated sync tool.
- Stripe combines sales, fees, and refunds into one lump-sum payout, and a clearing account in QuickBooks separates them, so a $96.80 deposit traces back to its $100 sale and $3.20 fee.
- Per Transaction sync keeps order-level detail for every charge, while Summary Sync posts one consolidated entry per day, payout, or custom period.
- A dedicated sync tool categorizes fees, records refunds, and closes open invoices automatically, which removes most manual entries.
- Most sync errors start at setup and cost less to prevent than to fix.


---


## **Does Stripe integrate with QuickBooks Online? Your connection options**


QuickBooks Online connects to Stripe through a connector app or a file import, not through a direct built-in link. There are five methods, and each records a different level of detail.


1. Bank feed only. You can connect Stripe to QuickBooks without an app by using the bank feed, but QuickBooks will only receive the payout as a single net deposit. Individual sales, fees, refunds, and other Stripe activity won’t be recorded separately.
2. Stripe Connector by QuickBooks. Intuit’s own QuickBooks integration with Stripe, listed in the QuickBooks App Store, queues sales, refunds, payouts, and fees for review in App transactions. It imports[up to 2 years of history and connects one Stripe account at a time](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/manage-integrations/connect-manage-stripe-transactions-quickbooks/L10TzOVcN_US_en_US) .
3. Middleware. Tools like Zapier map a Stripe event to a QuickBooks action, but you build and maintain the fee split, refunds, and payout matching yourself.
4. Dedicated sync tools.[Synder](https://synder.com/) , for example, syncs charges, fees, refunds, and payouts as separate records through a direct API connection, and adds a clearing account and multichannel sync. Synder’s research of 1K+ businesses showed that 16.3% had already tried another automation tool, rising to 25.2% in retail.
5. Manual CSV import. You export Stripe to QuickBooks as CSV files and upload them with the QuickBooks import tool or SaaSant Transactions. This suits one-time catch-ups, not ongoing sync.


The table compares all five methods side by side.


**Method** **What reaches QuickBooks** **Fee detail** **Clearing account** **Fits best when**


Bank feed only One net deposit per payout None No Volume is very low and you can split payouts by hand


Stripe Connector by QuickBooks Sales, refunds, payouts, and fees, queued for review in App transactions Posted to a Stripe Fees expense account Payout is recorded as a deposit linked to its sales and fees You have one Stripe account on QuickBooks Online and review each transaction


Middleware (such as Zapier) Only the records you configure Only if you build it Only if you build it Flows are simple and someone can maintain the Zaps


Dedicated sync tool (Synder) Separate sales, fees, refunds, and payouts, per transaction or as summaries A separate expense per charge, or a daily total Created automatically Volume is growing, you sell on several channels, or an accountant manages the books


Manual CSV import Whatever you upload Entered manually Set up manually You need a one-time catch-up of past data


### **What is the best way to connect Stripe and QuickBooks: native integration or third-party apps?**


Intuit’s connector or the bank feed can work for one Stripe account with light volume. If you need per-charge fee detail, several sales channels, or subscription billing, a dedicated tool is the better Stripe QuickBooks integration.


## **How does Stripe work with QuickBooks?**


Doesn’t matter what app you choose for the Stripe and QuickBooks connection, the integration workflow will be pretty much the same.


1. **Connecting Stripe to QuickBooks.** Users must first connect their Stripe account to QuickBooks. The setup usually involves logging into both your Stripe and QuickBooks accounts and authorizing the integration.


1. **Importing transactions.** Once you link Stripe to QuickBooks, all transactions, including sales, refunds, and other transaction types, are automatically imported.


1. **Handling fees and expenses.** Stripe charges processing fees for transactions, which are also recorded in QuickBooks during the integration. This ensures that all expenses related to Stripe transactions are accounted for.


1. **Categorizing and reconciling.** Imported transactions should be categorized and classified accurately. This helps reconcile books faster as transactions recorded in Stripe align with those in QuickBooks.


1. **Reporting.** With Stripe transactions recorded into QuickBooks, users can generate more comprehensive reports that include detailed insights from their payment processing activities.


*This is only a general overview of what the integration workflow between Stripe and QuickBooks might look like. The steps for how to link Stripe to QuickBooks can vary depending on your chosen third-party solution. We’ll discuss Stripe and QuickBooks connection in more detail below, using[Synder](https://synder.com/why-synder/) as an example of a third-party connector between the two platforms.*


## **When to consider the Stripe and QuickBooks connection**


Connecting Stripe with QuickBooks Online makes sense once manual bookkeeping can’t keep up with your Stripe volume. These five signs show you’ve reached that point.


**1. You need real-time financial visibility**
Sales, cash flow, and reports lag behind actual activity, making it harder to evaluate performance or react to changes quickly. An automated Stripe QuickBooks Online sync keeps sales and fees current in your reports.


**2. Reconciliation is taking too long**
In Synder’s research of over 1K businesses, 41.5% named manual data entry as their top accounting challenge, followed by confusion over fees and payouts (33.6%) and reconciliation issues (30.4%).


**3. Data accuracy is starting to slip**
As transaction volume grows, manual entry increases the risk of missing, duplicated, or misclassified transactions in your QuickBooks Stripe records.


**4. Tax prep requires too much cleanup**


Transactions need rework at period end because sales and expenses aren’t consistently categorized, slowing down filings and reviews.


**5. Lump-sum Stripe deposits don’t match individual sales**


Stripe pays out the total of many sales minus fees and refunds, so your bank shows one deposit that matches no single order. If you split these deposits by hand every week, a sync tool can do that work for you.

After automating the sync and categorization with Synder’s Smart Rules, the team reports saving time and money.

## **How do I sync Stripe records in QuickBooks?**


Here’s how to sync Stripe with QuickBooks Online: click “ *Ready to sync* ” next to the payment in the Synder dashboard.


Once the status is changed to “ *Synced* ”, it means that the transaction has been recorded in QuickBooks Online, and you can check the result by clicking the link “ *Show in QB* ”:


All the transaction details will be recorded in QuickBooks Online, including customer name, shipping address, product names, quantity, taxes, and discounts.[Sales tax posts to the correct tax liability account](https://synder.com/integrations/quickbooks/stripe/) rather than to income.


Product-level detail carries over when you connect Stripe to QuickBooks Online through Synder. By default, Synder will try to recognize your products from the payment system and match them to the items you’ve set up in QuickBooks Online. This way, your sales will automatically be categorized by the Income account assigned to certain products. If you’re tracking inventory, it will also be updated accordingly.


### **How do I categorize Stripe payments in QuickBooks?**


Synder categorizes Stripe payments in QuickBooks automatically, with separate settings for income and expenses.


### **Option #1. How to categorize income in QuickBooks**


There are two ways of setting up the automated categorization of income in QuickBooks Online.


**1. Categorize transactions in different income accounts based on the product names**


*Make sure that the product name in your payment processor matches the one in QuickBooks Online.*


When syncing a transaction, the Synder app automatically matches the product with the same name in QuickBooks and assigns the newly recorded transaction to the income account with the exact same name.


**If the names of the products differ** , you can use a Product Mapping feature to add different options of naming the same product across platforms. Go to “ *Settings* ” → “ *Configure* ” under Stripe → “ *Products/Services”* → “ *Product mapping”* . Each mapped name points to one item in your QuickBooks Products and Services list, and that item’s income account decides where the revenue posts.


**If the product has already been synced and assigned to the wrong account** , you can change it manually in QuickBooks. Just go to the “ *Sales* ” → “ *Products & Services* ’ tab and click “ *Edit* ” on the line of the wrongly recorded product. Change the income account to the needed one and save.


**2. Categorize all income transactions to one income account**


For this option, you’ll need to edit your Synder app settings.


Go to “ *Settings* ” → “ *Configure* ” under Stripe → “ *Products/Services* ”. Here you need to enable “ *Generic product* ” and select the product name from the list.


Once you update the app settings, all the newly synced transactions from Stripe will be synchronized under the chosen default name.


### **Option #2. How to apply categories to expenses in QuickBooks**


Smart Rules assign Stripe fees to different expense categories based on conditions such as the fee amount. For example, you sell two products which cost $20 and $400. You want to record the fees from both of them to different categories:


- The $20 product → Commissions & Fees category;
- The $400 product → Legal & Professional Fees.


What assumptions can be made? Well, it seems that the fee amount for the first product will probably be <$10. The fee for the second product will hardly be less than $10, so $10>.


Now, let’s create the flow of how the fees will be recorded based on the categorization rule:


1. **Go to** *Smart Rules* → *Rules → Create Rule;*
2. **Choose the trigger for the rule:** *Expense → Created;*
3. **Choose the condition:** *if Total amount → Less or equals → 10;*
4. **Choose the action:** *QuickBooks action → Expense → Update category* .


Enter the category name and repeat the action for the cases when the condition isn’t met.


After that, each time the Synder app generates an expense in your QuickBooks account, this Rule will become active.

## **How do I handle Stripe fees** ?


Synder records each Stripe fee in QuickBooks as an expense in a dedicated Stripe Fees account. Stripe deducts processing and service fees from each payment, and tracking them correctly is critical for accurate profit and reconciliation. Fees typically include processing (2.9% + 30¢), plus extras like international cards, currency conversion, disputes, instant payouts, and ACH transfers.


**How fees sync to accounting systems when you connect Stripe to QuickBooks:**


- **QuickBooks Online** – fees sync as Expenses
- **QuickBooks Desktop** – fees sync as Checks


Most standard Stripe accounts show fees embedded in sales transactions, while custom contracts or advanced Stripe features may list fees as separate line items.


**Fee categorization and visibility:** **** Synder captures every Stripe fee and posts it to a dedicated account (for example, Stripe Fees). Per Transaction sync shows fees per sale for precise cost tracking, while Summary Sync aggregates daily fees into a single expense entry. Smart Rules can also route different fee types to separate accounts.


**Example of the reconciliation flow:** **** For a $100 sale with a $3.20 fee:


- $100 recorded as income
- $3.20 recorded as a fee expense
- $96.80 deposited to the bank


This keeps revenue, fees, and payouts fully aligned. At the same rate, a $1,000 sale carries a $29.30 fee and a $970.70 payout.


### **What to do with Stripe balance reserves**


Synder records Stripe balance reserves in a separate reserve asset account and moves the funds back when Stripe releases them, typically after 30-180 days. Reserves are funds Stripe holds temporarily, and they reduce current payouts.


This ensures your clearing account always matches Stripe’s available balance and makes reconciliation predictable and accurate.


## **How do I deal with invoices** ?


Synder syncs each Stripe invoice to QuickBooks as an open invoice when it’s issued and closes it when payment arrives, which keeps accounts receivable accurate under accrual accounting.


If your business uses accrual accounting, Stripe invoices need to appear in QuickBooks as open accounts receivable when they’re issued, not when they’re paid. This keeps your A/R aging report accurate and records revenue in the period you earned it.


Synder manages the full invoice lifecycle, from creation to payment matching, while keeping accounts receivable accurate, even in edge cases like credit notes and failed payments.


The scenarios below cover how Synder handles invoice timing, refunds, payment matching, and common edge cases when you sync Stripe with QuickBooks invoices.


- **Invoice dates:** Stripe invoices have both a created date and a finalized (issued) date. Synder tracks both and can use either, which matters when drafts are created well before being sent.
- **Credit notes on paid invoices:** If a refund is issued via a credit note, Synder syncs the original invoice, payment, and refund. Credit notes issued *after* an invoice is already synced may require a rollback and resync. Best practice: issue credit notes before syncing invoices.
- **Automated payment matching:** Synder matches Stripe payments to invoices using customer data, invoice numbers, amounts, and dates. It supports partial payments, overpayments (as customer credits), and automatically closes fully paid invoices.
- **Customer matching flexibility:** You can control how customers are matched using priority fields such as name, email, billing/shipping details, or custom mappings to handle inconsistent data.
- **Payments without products:** If a Stripe payment has no product, Synder uses a default product or can pull the product name from the transaction description. Smart Rules can further automate categorization.

Synder’s study of 150+ SaaS businesses demonstrated that 91.5% used Stripe as their payment processor, which makes the Stripe QuickBooks Online integration a core part of their month-end close.

### **How to automate revenue recognition for Stripe subscriptions**


You automate revenue recognition for Stripe subscriptions with software that builds ASC 606 schedules from Stripe data and posts monthly journal entries from deferred revenue to income. An annual plan paid upfront is a liability (deferred, or unearned, revenue) until you deliver the service, so one-twelfth is recognized each month. This timing is a common pain point: 45.8% of SaaS businesses in Synder’s research named revenue recognition as a challenge, nearly 3 times the cross-industry average of 15.9%.


[Synder RevRec](https://synder.com/industry/revenue-recognition/) builds these schedules from Stripe data or an Excel upload and adjusts them for upgrades, cancellations, and prorations. In QuickBooks Online, Smart Rules can set the class, location, or account on each RevRec journal entry line. Stripe’s monthly recurring revenue (MRR) shows what customers are billed, while recognized revenue shows what you’ve earned, so your P&L should follow the recognized figure.


### **How to sync mixed Stripe payment types**


Synder syncs mixed Stripe payment types by type: invoice payments are applied to their Stripe invoice in QuickBooks, standalone charges sync as sales receipts, and Smart Rules can route each type to its own income account. This helps teams that move billing from QuickBooks to Stripe and end up with subscriptions, one-time charges, and manual invoices in one account.


## **How do I reconcile Stripe in QuickBooks** ?


You reconcile Stripe in QuickBooks by routing all Stripe activity through a clearing account, which ensures your sales, fees, and bank deposits line up correctly. The process relies on one key concept: the clearing account, which tracks money as it moves from Stripe to your bank.


### **Why Stripe bank deposits don’t match your sales**


Stripe bank deposits don’t match your sales because Stripe groups sales, refunds, and fees into one payout,[usually every business day](https://docs.stripe.com/payouts) , and deposits only the net amount. Each payout has a[Stripe payout ID](https://docs.stripe.com/payouts/reconciliation) , and Stripe’s[payout reconciliation report](https://docs.stripe.com/reports/payout-reconciliation) lists every charge, refund, and fee inside it, while unpaid charges sit in the pending balance. The clearing account below applies that breakdown to any Stripe integration with QuickBooks Online.


### **The clearing account: how reconciliation works**


A clearing account acts as a temporary holding account for Stripe activity. It separates gross sales, fees, and payouts, so bank deposits reconcile cleanly.


**Why it’s required:** Stripe payouts don’t equal sales totals because fees are deducted and funds are delayed. Without a clearing account, your books would show revenue that never hits the bank.


**Example ($100 sale, $3.20 fee):**


1. Record sale:


- Income: $100
- Stripe clearing: $100


2. Record fee:


- Stripe fees expense: $3.20
- Stripe clearing: –$3.20


3. Record payout:


- Bank account: $96.80
- Stripe clearing: –$96.80


After payout, the clearing account returns to zero (or reflects only unpaid transactions). With this setup in place, Synder users report that reconciliation drops from several hours to under 30 minutes.


**What to monitor regularly:**


- Stripe clearing balance should match Stripe’s *available balance.*
- Differences usually indicate unsynced transactions, timing delays, or duplicates.
- This balance is the fastest way to confirm your Stripe and QuickBooks integration is recording everything accurately.


***Note on reconciliation frequency:*** Reconcile weekly for high-volume or multi-channel sales, monthly for standard reporting, and monitor your Synder dashboard regularly to catch issues early.


### **Step-by-step reconciliation process**


Once your clearing account is set up, follow these steps to reconcile Stripe activity in QuickBooks without manual cleanup.


1. **Confirm all Stripe activity is synced** **** In Synder, check that all transactions for the period show *“Synced”* . Resolve failed or pending items first.
2. **Verify the clearing account balance** **** The Stripe clearing account balance in QuickBooks should match Stripe’s available balance, allowing for processing delays.
3. **Review payout transactions** **** Ensure each Stripe payout matches the transferred amount, has the correct date, and is synced to QuickBooks.
4. **Match payouts to bank deposits** **** In QuickBooks Banking, locate Stripe deposits and match them to transfers from the Stripe clearing account, confirming the amount and direction (Clearing → Bank).
5. **Resolve unmatched deposits** **** If no match appears, use *“Find match,”* check for date differences, and confirm the payout was synced and not already matched.
6. **Reconcile the bank account** **** Run the standard QuickBooks reconciliation, confirming the statement balance and date match, Stripe payouts are already matched, and the ending difference is $0.00.
7. **Final clearing account check** **** After reconciliation, confirm the Stripe clearing account balance is $0.00. Any remaining balance represents funds not yet paid out by Stripe.


## **Common mistakes when connecting Stripe to QuickBooks and how to fix them**


Most problems with a Stripe and QuickBooks setup come from a few avoidable choices made before the first sync, plus a few issues that show up later during reconciliation.


**Setup mistakes**


- Posting the same sales from Shopify and Stripe. *Solution:* Use one source per sale. In Synder, connect Shopify and Stripe together so Stripe payments match their Shopify orders.
- Skipping the clearing account. *Solution:* Post Stripe sales to a Stripe clearing account, not to checking or Undeposited Funds, so gross sales, fees, and net payouts stay separate.
- Importing history without a cutoff date. *Solution:* Before you import Stripe into QuickBooks Online for past periods, start the day after your old method last recorded Stripe activity.


According to Synder’s analysis, fixing errors in the general ledger costs 5 to 10 times more than catching them before the sync.


**Reconciliation issues after setup**


Even with automated syncing, QuickBooks Stripe reconciliation issues can still appear due to timing differences, reserves, or missed adjustments. Knowing what to look for makes these problems quick to resolve instead of time-consuming investigations.


- Payout amounts don’t match bank deposits. *Solution:* Check for Stripe balance reserves that temporarily hold funds, and confirm instant payout fees are recorded as separate expenses.
- Old transactions sitting in the clearing account. *Solution:* These are often refunds or chargebacks tied to earlier sales. Sync the related adjustment transactions from Stripe to bring the clearing account back to zero.
- Duplicate transactions appear. *Solution:* Use Synder’s rollback feature to remove incorrect entries, then resync the transaction cleanly. Duplicate detection prevents most cases, but rollback ensures accuracy when issues slip through. If duplicates are already in QuickBooks, fix them in this order:


1. Pause auto-sync in Synder.
2. Find and disconnect the second source, such as Stripe Connector by QuickBooks, a Shopify accounting app, or a bank rule that auto-adds Stripe deposits.
3. Identify each duplicate by its Stripe charge ID (ch_) and check the QuickBooks Audit Log for the app that created it.
4. Roll back Synder duplicates, and delete (don’t void) the other app’s copies, since voided entries stay in reports at $0.
5. Resume sync and confirm the clearing balance matches Stripe’s available balance.


- Clearing account doesn’t match Stripe’s available balance. *Solution:* Review failed syncs, manual entries, or unsupported transaction types. Synder’s sync logs help pinpoint missing or errored transactions quickly.


And keep in mind that with a proper clearing account setup and automated syncing, reconciliation shifts from a multi-hour cleanup to a quick, routine check.

## **FAQ**


### **Integration basics**


#### **Does Stripe connect to QuickBooks directly?**


Stripe doesn’t integrate directly with QuickBooks Online, so a connector app is required to sync sales, fees, invoices, and payouts between the two systems. Options for how to connect Stripe to QuickBooks Online include Intuit’s Stripe Connector by QuickBooks and third-party tools like Synder. The right one depends on how much detail you need in your books.


#### **Does Stripe sync with QuickBooks Online automatically?**


Stripe syncs with QuickBooks Online automatically once a connector app is in place. Synder, for example, imports new Stripe transactions hourly on Essential and higher plans, and daily on Basic. Intuit’s Stripe Connector by QuickBooks usually shows new transactions within 2 hours, but it can’t be updated on demand.


#### **Can Stripe replace QuickBooks?**


Stripe can’t replace QuickBooks, because Stripe processes payments while QuickBooks keeps the general ledger for all your income, expenses, bills, and bank accounts. Most businesses use both, with a connector syncing Stripe activity into QuickBooks. You don’t need Stripe to use QuickBooks, since QuickBooks Payments also accepts cards, but Stripe is common for online checkout and subscription billing.


#### **What accounting software integrates with Stripe?**


Stripe connects to accounting systems like QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop, Xero, Sage Intacct, NetSuite, and Zoho Books through third-party apps. Stripe doesn’t offer native accounting integrations.


#### **Does Stripe integrate with QuickBooks Desktop or only QuickBooks Online?**


Stripe can sync with both QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Desktop, depending on the connector. Most connectors, including Intuit’s Stripe Connector by QuickBooks, are built for Online. Synder supports Desktop on Essential plans and higher. Features such as real-time sync may differ on Desktop, so confirm before choosing how to integrate Stripe with QuickBooks Online or Desktop.


### **Setup and troubleshooting**


#### **Will connecting Stripe to QuickBooks create duplicate entries if Shopify is already syncing to QBO?**


Connecting Stripe to QuickBooks creates duplicate entries only when two apps post the same sale, such as a Shopify accounting app and a Stripe connection. Shopify Payments is powered by Stripe, so this overlap is common. Use one source per sale: in Synder, Shopify Payments comes in through your Shopify connection, so disconnect any other app that posts those orders.


#### **What are the most common mistakes when setting up a Stripe-to-QuickBooks integration?**


The three most common setup mistakes are posting the same sale from two apps, skipping the clearing account, and importing history without a cutoff date. The “Common mistakes” section above explains how to fix each one.


#### **Can I connect multiple Stripe accounts or Stripe Connect to one QuickBooks file?**


You can connect multiple Stripe accounts, and Stripe Connect platform accounts, to one QuickBooks file with Synder. Each account gets its own clearing account, and Synder records Connect fees separately. Intuit’s Stripe Connector supports one Stripe account at a time.


#### **How do I import historical Stripe transactions into QuickBooks Online?**


You import historical Stripe transactions into QuickBooks Online by setting a start date in Synder’s historical import, beginning the day after your old method last recorded Stripe activity. You can also import Stripe data into QuickBooks from CSV files and enter fees manually.


### **Features and automation**


#### **Can I automatically sync Stripe invoices to QuickBooks?**


Stripe invoices can sync to QuickBooks automatically through a dedicated tool such as Synder, which applies payments to open invoices and closes them without manual matching. It’s one of the best ways to sync Stripe with QuickBooks invoices without manual entry.


#### **How do I record Stripe fees in QuickBooks Online?**


Stripe fees should be recorded as expenses. Integration tools can automatically create fee transactions in QuickBooks, while manual entry requires downloading Stripe reports and posting expenses yourself.


#### **How do I automate revenue recognition for Stripe subscriptions in QuickBooks Online?**


Automate revenue recognition for Stripe subscriptions with a tool such as[Synder RevRec](https://synder.com/industry/revenue-recognition/) , which creates ASC 606 schedules from Stripe subscription data and posts monthly journal entries from deferred revenue to income. Schedules adjust for upgrades, cancellations, and prorations. The SaaS section above shows how each event is recorded.


#### **How do I handle multi-currency Stripe transactions when syncing to QuickBooks?**


To handle multi-currency Stripe transactions, turn on Multicurrency in QuickBooks Online first, since it can’t be turned off later. Synder records each transaction in its original currency and converts it with the platform’s rate, and QuickBooks posts rate differences to Exchange Gain or Loss. Map each payout currency to its own clearing and bank account.
